what_worked: Power-law distribution insight and signal-vs-noise correlation framing show genuine analytical engagement with the dataset.
fix_next: The $134M revenue figure is ~8.6× the actual $15.6M total; this foundational error undermines every downstream claim and valuation logic.
verdict: Ambitious pitch narrative built on a fabricated revenue total and thin dataset engagement.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: '$134M verified 12-month operating revenue' — actual 30-day total is $15.6M; even annualized ~$187M, not $134M, and annualizing 30-day data is methodologically unsound. Slide 6: Median MRR $282 and Mean MRR $13,472 are presented without clear denominators or filters; dataset-wide median/mean of 30-day revenue don't match these cleanly. Slide 10: Stripe shown as 64% — actual is 63.6% (636/1000), acceptable rounding, but the text says '258 US startups' using Stripe when reference says 221 US Stripe users out of 258 US total. Slide 3: '262 startups actively listed for sale with disclosed multiples' is unverifiable from the dataset description provided.

evidence.insight: Slide 5-6 identify zero-revenue prevalence and power-law skew; slide 7 contrasts signal (subscriptions r≈0.91) vs noise (vanity metrics). These are real analytical moves, but most slides repackage observations as strategy rather than deepening analysis.
evidence.narrative: Coherent arc from market opportunity → dataset advantage → filtering logic → build+buy strategy → ask. However, it reads as an investment pitch, not a data story; the dataset serves as decoration for a pre-formed thesis rather than driving discovery.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 frames audience as investors, but the assignment is a data-story presentation. No mention of dataset limitations (241 missing country, 274 missing category, 288 missing audience_type). No source citations for external claims (41% CAGR, $109B investment).
evidence.accuracy: Slide 3's $134M is the most damaging error — off by ~8.6× from the actual $15.6M 30-day total. Slide 10 conflates 258 (total US startups) with 258 US Stripe users (actual is 221). The correlation claims (r≈0.91, r≈0.87) are plausible but unverifiable and presented without caveats. Founded-year correlation is never mentioned despite being essentially zero.
evidence.visual: Clean, consistent template with good hierarchy and restrained color palette. Charts are simple but legible. Slide 10 has a text duplication bug ('for ing, we possess'). The infinity-loop diagram on slide 7 is decorative rather than informative. Overall professional but repetitive layout.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy consulting-speak throughout: 'unfair advantage,' 'asymmetric target,' 'dual-engine strategy,' 'seamlessly integrating into a singular SaaS ecosystem.' Slide 9 bottom text is classic AI filler. The infinity loop on slide 7 is decorative-but-meaningless. Template sameness across slides.
